assumptions.choice: Use an online AR(1) model of close-to-close returns, trained by gradient descent after each observed return; a positive or negative next-return forecast denotes predicted price increase or decrease.
assumptions.reason: The specification requires autoregressive learning with gradient descent but does not specify model order, features, initialization, or learning rate.

assumptions.choice: Use a fixed learning rate of 0.01.
Interpret the stated histogram crossing its signal line literally by comparing MACD histogram values with the MACD signal-line values on consecutive bars.
assumptions.reason: A standard MACD histogram is normally derived from the signal line rather than independently paired with it, but the specification explicitly requires this comparison.

assumptions.choice: Use population standard deviation of the latest 20 closing prices and compare it with the mean of all prior computed 20-period volatility values; do not enter until at least one prior volatility value exists.
assumptions.reason: The specification does not define the price field, standard-deviation convention, historical averaging window, or initial baseline behavior.

assumptions.choice: Evaluate take-profit and stop-loss conditions using the current bar close against the executed entry price.
assumptions.reason: The specification gives percentage thresholds but does not state whether intrabar high/low prices or closing prices trigger them.

assumptions.choice: Use the largest whole-share position whose market value at the current close is no more than 1% of current broker equity.
assumptions.reason: The specification caps each position at 1% of total trading capital but does not define rounding or whether capital is static or mark-to-market.
